findings.title: Substring match for event.type:error also matches negated and mixed queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the lowercased query contains the substring `event.type:error`. That also matches `!event.type:error`, which excludes errors, and mixed queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. For the discover dataset this applies `upsampled_count()` (sum of sample_weight) to queries that return transactions or other non-error events. Those rows have no sample_weight, so the reported counts are wrong. The query should be parsed properly instead of substring-matched.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility checks the outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` passes the closed-over request-level `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, not the `scoped_dataset` actually being queried. In the dashboard split path, `scoped_dataset` is `discover` with an `!event.type:transaction` errors query while the outer `dataset` is a metrics dataset. The check then never upsamples the errors split. The opposite mismatch is also possible: the decision is made for one dataset and the transformed columns run against another.

findings.title: Allowlist cache makes changes stale and is never invalidated
findings.body: Eligibility is cached for 60s in the shared cache. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but nothing calls it, so allowlist changes take up to 60s to apply. The `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` docstring says it 'reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time', which is false once this cache is in front of it. In tests that mock `options`, a value cached by one test can leak into the next test when the same project IDs recur, giving order-dependent results.

findings.title: Cache round-trip runs before the cheap dataset check and may cost more than it saves
findings.body: `options.get` is already locally cached, so replacing it with a remote cache get/set (memcached/redis) on every `_get_event_stats` call likely adds latency rather than removing it. The lookup also runs before `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, so requests for spans, transactions or metrics datasets pay for the cache round-trip even though they can never be upsampled.

findings.title: upsampled_count silently undercounts events without sample_weight
findings.body: `sum(sample_weight)` ignores NULLs, so any event in an allowlisted project that lacks sample_weight counts as 0 instead of 1. Examples are events ingested before the rollout or without client sampling context. The comment assumes the schema guarantees the column is populated, which is not enforced anywhere. Use something like `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` so missing weights count as one event.

findings.title: Top-events ordering and selected fields are not transformed
findings.body: For top events only `timeseries_columns` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()`. `selected_columns` (from `get_field_list`) and `orderby` still use raw `count()`. The top-N groups are therefore chosen by raw count while the plotted values are upsampled, so the two can disagree.

findings.title: Accidental submodule gitlink committed
findings.body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink (a subproject pointing at the base commit). It has no `.gitmodules` entry and is unrelated to the feature, so it looks like it was committed by mistake. It will confuse checkouts and tooling and should be removed.

findings.title: No tests for the cached entry point or negated queries
findings.body: The unit tests never exercise `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, so the caching behaviour and cache-key logic are untested. They also do not cover negated or mixed queries such as `!event.type:error` for `_is_error_focused_query`, which is exactly where the substring heuristic fails.
